title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: AI-powered investigation of policy sync and device health
summary: The briefing accurately separates Microsoft's planned AI investigation capability from the existing device troubleshooting tools. The roadmap details and documented controls are supported; searches found no feature-specific licensing, default state or enablement instructions.

claims.claim: The planned capability belongs to Microsoft Purview Endpoint Data Loss Prevention.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention - Policy Sync & Device Health AI-Powered Investigation

claims.claim: Microsoft plans AI-powered visibility into DLP policy deployment to help administrators track synchronization progress and enforcement coverage.
claims.quote: AI-powered visibility into DLP policy deployment across devices, helping admins track sync progress and understand enforcement coverage.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant UI switch or API to enable, disable or scope this AI investigation capability is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Endpoint DLP policy sync device health AI investigation default enabled roles tenant switch; opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/copilot-in-purview-overview and learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync. No feature-specific switch or API found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Per-device configuration and policy sync status are reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Settings > Device onboarding > Devices.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices.

claims.claim: Microsoft Defender portal Advanced hunting supports the query DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" | project DlpInfo.
claims.quote:
Go to the Microsoft Defender portal
Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting
Query the DeviceInfo table
Sample query:
DeviceInfo
| where DlpInfo != ""
| project DlpInfo

claims.claim: The device health reports dashboard is reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Settings > Device onboarding > Device report.
claims.quote:
Go to the Microsoft Purview portal.
Select Settings > Device onboarding > Device report.

claims.claim: No API or automation equivalent for the device health reports dashboard is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "device health reports dashboard" API PowerShell readiness; "Purview" "device health reports" "API". Opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/device-onboarding-health-reports-dashboard and the Purview APIs overview; no equivalent dashboard API found.

claims.claim: Learn places the overall Policy status report at Data loss prevention > Overview, using the Microsoft Purview compliance portal name as the note explains.
claims.quote: The Policy status report is available in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal on the > Data loss prevention > Overview page.

claims.claim: No API or automation equivalent for the overall Policy status report is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "Policy status" report "PowerShell"; "Endpoint DLP" "policy sync" "API" report. Opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync and the Purview APIs overview; found device-level KQL, not an overall Policy status report endpoint.

claims.claim: Existing device views expose configuration status and policy sync status for onboarded devices as status information administrators can inspect.
claims.quote: Configuration status and the Policy sync status of all your onboarded devices have three possible values.

claims.claim: The existing device health reports dashboard summarizes device readiness for policy updates and Endpoint DLP features.
claims.quote: Use the dashboard to monitor device onboarding status, policy update readiness, and feature readiness for Endpoint DLP.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access to the existing device health reports dashboard requires Compliance Administrator, Security Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote:
To access the device health reporting dashboard, you must have one of the following roles:
Compliance Administrator
Security Administrator
Global Administrator

claims.claim: Learn recommends least privilege and identifies Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator as sufficient for most organizations using the dashboard.
claims.quote: Use the least-privileged role that meets your needs. For most organizations, the Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator role is sufficient.

claims.claim: The dashboard's policy-update readiness indicators identify risk of missing future updates rather than confirming a failed update.
claims.quote: These indicators don't confirm whether a device failed to receive a policy update, but instead highlight devices that may be at risk of not receiving future updates.

claims.claim: Devices represented by the device health dashboard must be onboarded to Endpoint DLP.
claims.quote:
Devices must also:
Be onboarded to Endpoint DLP

claims.claim: The device health dashboard requires devices to be actively reporting device telemetry.
claims.quote:
Devices must also:
Be onboarded to Endpoint DLP
Be actively reporting device telemetry

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP monitors sensitive-item activity on onboarded devices and can enforce protective actions on those items.
claims.quote: Once devices are onboarded into the Microsoft Purview solutions, the information about what users are doing with sensitive items is made visible in activity explorer. You can then enforce protective actions on those items via DLP policies.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can monitor onboarded Windows 10 devices.
claims.quote: Microsoft Endpoint DLP allows you to monitor onboarded Windows 10, and Windows 11

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can monitor onboarded Windows 11 devices.
claims.quote: Microsoft Endpoint DLP allows you to monitor onboarded Windows 10, and Windows 11

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can monitor onboarded macOS devices running one of the three latest released versions.
claims.quote: and onboarded macOS devices running any of the three latest released versions.

claims.claim: A device must receive a policy before that policy can protect it.
claims.quote: Policies that are updated while a device is offline won't be pushed to that device. Similarly, such policies won't be enforced on that device, until the device is back online.

claims.claim: Devices must be online for policy updates to occur.
claims.quote: Devices must be online for the policy update to happen. If the status isn't updating, check the last time the device was seen.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A Policy sync status of Not updated means the device has not synchronized the latest policy updates.
claims.quote: Not updated | This device isn't synced the latest policy updates.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Policies updated while a device is offline are not pushed to it, while its existing outdated policy continues to be enforced.
claims.quote: Policies that are updated while a device is offline won't be pushed to that device. Similarly, such policies won't be enforced on that device, until the device is back online. However, the outdated policy that exists on the offline device will still be enforced.

claims.claim: The status in the devices list can take up to two hours to update.
claims.quote: It might take up to 2 hours for the status in the devices list to update.

claims.claim: Configuration status includes checks of Microsoft Defender Antivirus always-on protection.
claims.quote: For Windows devices, configuration includes checking the status of Microsoft Defender Antivirus always-on protection and behavior monitoring.

claims.claim: Configuration status includes checks of Microsoft Defender Antivirus behavior monitoring.
claims.quote: For Windows devices, configuration includes checking the status of Microsoft Defender Antivirus always-on protection and behavior monitoring.

claims.claim: The existing device attributes include the time the device was last seen online.
claims.quote: Last seen | The most recent time that the device was determined to be online.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn provides troubleshooting remediation steps in the device details pane and a workflow diagram.
claims.quote: If the status is Not updated or Not available, follow the remediation steps in the details pane and the steps in the workflow diagram.

claims.claim: The device health dashboard helps administrators identify misconfigured devices.
claims.quote: Use the dashboard to monitor device posture at scale, find misconfigured devices, detect devices that might not receive Endpoint DLP policy updates, and validate readiness before deploying new features.

claims.claim: Learn recommends investigating devices that have not reported recently.
claims.quote: Investigate devices that haven't reported recently. Devices offline for extended periods may miss critical policy updates.

claims.claim: Learn recommends prioritizing remediation for devices with outdated Defender versions.
claims.quote: Prioritize remediation for devices with outdated Defender versions. Outdated Microsoft Defender Antivirus versions can prevent devices from receiving Endpoint DLP policies.

claims.claim: Not available is a possible Policy sync status for onboarded devices.
claims.quote: System shows Not available if there is no Endpoint DLP policy.
